description: The TuriX-CUA Multimodal Vision Pipeline adds visual AI capabilities to qontinui's agentic verification loop. When users run workflows with agentic verification architecture, the system can capture screenshots, annotate them with numbered element markers, and send annotated images to vision-capable LLMs (Claude API, Gemini API) for screen analysis. A two-phase Brain/Actor pattern splits expensive vision reasoning from cheap action execution. This spec covers the pages where these capabilities are configured (Settings > AI, Run Options Dialog), where results are displayed (Run Summary, Active Dashboard, AI Output), and where supporting features surface (Skills page for playbooks, action executor for click highlights). Data flows from the Rust backend through Tauri IPC commands to the React frontend.

groups.name: Vision Feature Page Reachability
groups.description: Users access vision pipeline configuration and results across several existing pages. The AI provider settings page is where multimodal support is configured. The Run Options Dialog is where agentic verification architecture (including Brain/Actor) is selected before running a workflow. Run detail pages show the results. These are all existing pages that now carry additional data from the vision pipeline.

assertions.description: The Settings > AI page is reachable from the sidebar navigation. Users navigate here to configure which AI provider is active (Claude CLI, Claude API, Gemini CLI, Gemini API). Only API providers (Claude API, Gemini API) support multimodal vision prompts

The Run Options Dialog is reachable when launching a workflow from the workflow list. Users can select the workflow architecture (Traditional, Agentic Verification, Multi-Agent Pipeline) which determines whether the Brain/Actor vision pipeline is available
assertions.precondition: A workflow exists in the workflow list and the user has opened the Run Options Dialog for it

assertions.description: The Run Summary page is reachable from the History/Runs list by clicking a completed run. This is where Brain/Actor iteration results, annotated screenshots, and verification verdicts are displayed after a workflow completes
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow run has completed

groups.name: AI Provider Settings Elements
groups.description: The Settings > AI page contains controls for selecting the AI provider and configuring API keys. The provider choice determines whether multimodal (vision) prompts are supported. Data is read and written via Tauri IPC commands (get_ai_settings, save_ai_settings) backed by settings.rs in the Rust backend. API keys are stored in the OS keychain via the keyring crate.

assertions.description: The page shows a provider selection control with four options: Claude Code CLI, Claude API, Gemini CLI, and Gemini API. Each option has a label and a radio button or equivalent selector
The Claude API provider option is present. When selected, this provider sends multimodal content blocks (text + image) to the Claude Messages API at https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages
When an API provider (Claude API or Gemini API) is selected, the page shows an API key input field. The field masks the key value and has a save button
assertions.precondition: An API provider (Claude API or Gemini API) is selected as the active provider

assertions.description: The page shows a model selector or text input for the AI model ID. For Claude API this accepts model IDs like claude-opus-4-6, claude-sonnet-4-6. For Gemini API this accepts IDs like gemini-2.5-pro
The page shows a test/verify button that validates the API key and model configuration by making a test call to the provider

groups.name: AI Provider Settings Interactions
groups.description: Users interact with the AI settings to configure which provider powers their automation. Switching providers affects whether multimodal vision features work (API providers support images, CLI providers fall back to text-only).

assertions.description: Users can switch the active AI provider by clicking a different provider option. The page updates to show provider-specific configuration fields (API key fields for API providers, CLI path fields for CLI providers)
assertions.expected: Clicking a provider option selects it and reveals its configuration section. Previously shown sections for other providers collapse or hide. The selected state persists after navigating away and returning

assertions.description: Users can enter an API key and save it. The key is stored in the OS keychain via the keyring crate, not in plaintext config files
assertions.expected: After entering a key and clicking Save, a success indicator appears (toast, checkmark, or status text). The key field shows a masked value on subsequent page loads
assertions.precondition: An API provider is selected

assertions.description: Users can test the AI provider connection to verify their API key and model configuration work
assertions.expected: Clicking the test button shows a loading state, then either a success message with the model's response or an error message explaining what failed (invalid key, unreachable endpoint, invalid model ID)
assertions.precondition: An API provider is selected and an API key has been saved

groups.name: Workflow Architecture Selection
groups.description: When launching a workflow, users choose the execution architecture from the Run Options Dialog. The 'Agentic Verification' architecture enables the verification-agent/worker-agent loop where the Brain/Actor vision pipeline operates. The architecture choice is stored in the workflow's LoopConfig and sent to the Rust backend via the /run Tauri command.

assertions.description: The Run Options Dialog shows three architecture choices: Traditional (deterministic verification loop), Agentic Verification (AI verifier + AI worker loop), and Multi-Agent Pipeline (DAG-structured specialized agents)
assertions.precondition: The Run Options Dialog is open for a workflow

assertions.description: The Agentic Verification option has a description explaining it uses an AI verifier + AI worker reasoning loop. This is the architecture where Brain/Actor mode, annotated screenshots, and progressive memory compression are active
assertions.precondition: The Run Options Dialog is open for a workflow

groups.name: Agentic Verification Run Results Display
groups.description: After an agentic verification workflow completes, the Run Summary page displays per-iteration results. Each iteration shows the verification verdict (Pass/Fail/Partial with confidence percentage), worker summary, and timing. When Brain/Actor mode was active, iterations additionally show the Brain's screen analysis and action plan injected into the worker context. Data is fetched via Tauri IPC commands (get_task_run, get_task_run_events) reading from the PostgreSQL task_runs and task_run_events tables.

assertions.description: The page shows the overall run outcome prominently: goal_achieved (true/false), iterations_run count, and whether the run was stopped by the user or hit max_iterations
assertions.expected: A status banner or indicator at the top of the page shows one of: 'Goal Achieved' (green), 'Failed' (red), 'Stopped' (yellow), 'Max Iterations Reached' (orange). The iterations_run count appears as a number
assertions.precondition: At least one agentic verification workflow run has completed

assertions.description: Each iteration in the run shows the verification verdict with status and confidence. The confidence is displayed as a percentage derived from the verifier's 0.0-1.0 confidence score
assertions.expected: Each iteration row shows status text (Pass, Fail, Partial, or Unreachable) and a confidence percentage (e.g., '85%'). Pass verdicts at or above the confidence_threshold are highlighted positively
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run with at least 2 iterations has completed

assertions.description: Each iteration that ran a worker agent shows a summary of what the worker did, truncated to approximately 500 characters. This is the approach the AI took to address verification failures
assertions.expected: A text block under each iteration showing the worker's approach. Long summaries end with '...' indicating truncation
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run with at least 1 worker iteration has completed

assertions.description: When Brain/Actor mode was active during a run, the AI Output tab shows the Brain's visual analysis section within the worker context. This appears as a '## Visual Analysis (Brain Agent)' heading followed by the Brain's screen analysis, action plan, and element index
assertions.expected: The AI output for worker iterations contains a 'Visual Analysis (Brain Agent)' section with: a screen analysis paragraph, a numbered action plan, and an element index listing interactive elements with normalized coordinates

target.label: Brain analysis section in AI output

assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run with brain_actor_enabled:true has completed at least 1 iteration

assertions.description: The element index displayed in Brain/Actor run results lists detected interactive elements in the format: [N] "Label" type at (x, y) size (w, h) where coordinates are normalized 0.0-1.0 values
assertions.expected: A formatted list where each line starts with a bracketed number like [1], [2], etc., followed by a quoted label, element type, and normalized coordinate values between 0 and 1
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run with brain_actor_enabled:true has completed and the UI Bridge SDK was connected during execution

assertions.description: The run statistics or token usage section shows token counts broken down by phase. When Brain/Actor mode is active, Brain (multimodal) calls show higher input token counts due to image encoding compared to Actor (text-only) calls
assertions.expected: Token usage is displayed with input_tokens and output_tokens counts. Total cost in USD is shown based on model pricing
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow run has completed with an API provider configured

groups.name: Agentic Verification Loop Behavior
groups.description: The agentic verification loop runs iterations of verification-agent followed by worker-agent until the goal is achieved or max_iterations is reached. Key automatic behaviors include: progressive iteration history compression (keeps context under 4000 chars), consecutive pass tracking (requires N passes before declaring success), and stop-signal responsiveness. When Brain/Actor mode is enabled, the Brain is invoked with multimodal prompts when should_invoke_brain() returns true (first iteration, cache expired, or RequestContext signal). The loop is orchestrated by LoopController in unified_workflow_executor/agentic_verification_loop.rs.

assertions.description: The active dashboard shows iterations progressing in real time during an agentic verification run. Each iteration transitions through: verification agent running → verdict displayed → worker agent running → worker output displayed
assertions.expected: The iteration count increments as each iteration completes. The current phase (verifying/working) is indicated. New iterations appear without page refresh
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification workflow is currently running

assertions.description: Users can stop a running agentic verification workflow. The stop signal is checked at the start of each iteration. When stopped, the run result shows was_stopped:true and the iterations completed so far are preserved
assertions.expected: After clicking stop, the run transitions to a stopped state within one iteration. The run summary shows the iterations that completed before the stop
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification workflow is currently running

assertions.description: When the verification agent reports Pass with confidence above the threshold for the required number of consecutive passes, the loop exits with goal_achieved:true. The UI reflects this as a successful outcome
assertions.expected: The run transitions to complete status with a success indicator. The final verdict shows Pass with the confidence percentage. The consecutive pass count matches required_consecutive_passes from the config
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run has completed successfully (goal achieved)

assertions.description: When the loop reaches max_iterations without achieving the goal, it exits with max_iterations_reached:true. The UI shows this as a non-success outcome distinct from errors
assertions.expected: The run shows 'Max iterations reached' or similar status. The iterations_run count equals max_iterations. The final verdict is the last iteration's verdict (typically Fail or Partial)
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run has completed by hitting max_iterations

assertions.description: When the active AI provider is a CLI variant (Claude CLI, Gemini CLI), multimodal vision features are unavailable. If Brain/Actor mode is enabled, the system falls back to text-only Brain invocations and logs a warning
assertions.expected: No annotated screenshots appear in Brain/Actor iteration results. The runner logs contain a warning: 'does not support image content blocks; falling back to text-only'
assertions.precondition: A CLI provider is configured and an agentic verification run with brain_actor_enabled:true has completed

groups.name: Configuration-to-Execution State Consistency
groups.description: The UI must accurately reflect the relationship between configuration state (which provider is active, whether Brain/Actor is enabled) and execution results (whether multimodal was used, whether Brain analysis appears). Mismatches indicate bugs in the config propagation through the Tauri IPC layer.

assertions.description: The AI provider shown on the Settings > AI page matches the provider recorded in task run token usage. If Claude API is selected, run results show Claude API token usage; if Gemini CLI is selected, run results show Gemini CLI
assertions.expected: The provider name in run statistics matches the provider name on the settings page. Changing the provider and running a new workflow produces results with the new provider's name
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow run has completed with the current provider configuration

assertions.description: The workflow architecture selected in the Run Options Dialog determines the loop type shown in run results. 'Agentic Verification' produces iterations with verification verdicts and worker summaries. 'Traditional' produces setup/verification/agentic phase results without verdict confidence scores
assertions.expected: Runs started with 'Agentic Verification' show per-iteration verdicts with confidence percentages. Runs started with 'Traditional' show phase-based results without AI verdicts
assertions.precondition: At least one run of each architecture type has completed

assertions.description: The number of iteration panels or rows displayed in the run detail matches the iterations_run count reported in the run summary header
assertions.expected: If the summary says '5 iterations', exactly 5 iteration rows or panels are visible (possibly with pagination). No phantom or missing iterations
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run with 2+ iterations has completed

groups.name: Run Detail Interactions
groups.description: Users interact with run detail pages to inspect iteration results, view AI output, and continue failed runs. The Run Summary page uses tabs (Timeline, Verification, Knowledge, Context, Canvas, Errors) for deep dives. Data is fetched from the Rust backend via get_task_run and get_task_run_events Tauri commands.

assertions.description: Users can switch between the tabbed sections of the Run Summary to access different views of the run data. The Timeline tab shows chronological events, the Verification tab shows verification plans and results
assertions.expected: Clicking a tab label switches the visible content panel. The selected tab is visually highlighted. Tab content loads without a full page refresh
assertions.precondition: A completed run's summary page is open

assertions.description: Users can continue a finished (complete, failed, or stopped) agentic verification run by adding more sessions. This preserves the iteration history and context from previous iterations
assertions.expected: A 'Continue' button is visible on the run summary. Clicking it opens a dialog to specify additional sessions. After confirming, the run resumes from where it left off
assertions.precondition: A completed or stopped run's summary page is open

assertions.description: Users can view the full AI output for each iteration by navigating to the AI Output tab or expanding an iteration detail. This shows the complete prompt and response including any Brain/Actor visual analysis sections
assertions.expected: The AI Output section shows per-iteration conversation logs with the full prompt text (including injected context) and the AI's response. For Brain/Actor runs, the '## Visual Analysis (Brain Agent)' section is visible in the prompt
assertions.precondition: A completed run's summary page is open and the run had at least 1 agentic iteration

groups.name: Vision Pipeline Purpose and Mental Model
groups.description: The vision pipeline serves two user needs: (1) for developers automating their own web apps (UI Bridge white-box), it provides rich element data for intelligent verification without fragile selectors; (2) for automating third-party desktop apps (visual GUI black-box), it provides screenshot-based element detection with LLM vision reasoning. Users should understand which mode is active and why the system chose it.

assertions.description: The Agentic Verification architecture option communicates that it uses AI reasoning to assess goal achievement rather than hard-coded checks. Users understand this is for goals that are hard to verify deterministically (e.g., 'the page looks correct' vs 'HTTP status is 200')

The iteration history shown in run results communicates the progressive problem-solving approach: what was tried, what failed, and how the approach evolved. Users understand that older iterations are compressed to prevent context bloat while preserving key learnings
assertions.precondition: An agentic verification run with 3+ iterations has completed

assertions.description: The Skills page communicates that playbooks provide domain-specific knowledge for automating particular applications. Users understand that playbooks are human-editable markdown files stored in ~/.qontinui/playbooks/ that the system automatically includes when triggers match the current automation target

groups.name: Click Highlight Visual Design
groups.description: During automation execution, brief visual highlights appear at action locations (click, type, scroll targets). For UI Bridge apps, this is a CSS overlay injected by showClickHighlight() in debug/click-highlight.ts, called from action-executor.ts after each performAction() succeeds. Highlights use position:fixed, pointer-events:none, z-index:999999 to avoid interfering with the page. The animation is a pulsing circle that scales from 0.5 to 1.2 and fades from opacity 1 to 0 over 600ms.

assertions.description: Click highlights are color-coded by action type so users can distinguish what kind of action was performed at each location
assertions.expected: Click actions show green (#00c800) highlights, type/sendKeys actions show blue (#0064ff), scroll actions show orange (#ff8c00), select actions show purple (#b400b4), focus actions show teal (#00b4b4)
assertions.precondition: An action (click, type, etc.) has been executed via the UI Bridge action executor within the last 600ms

assertions.description: Click highlight overlays do not capture mouse events or block interaction with underlying elements. They exist purely as visual feedback
assertions.expected: The highlight div has CSS pointer-events:none. Clicking through the highlight area reaches the element underneath. The highlight is removed from the DOM after 600ms
assertions.precondition: An action has been executed via the UI Bridge action executor within the last 600ms

states.name: AI Settings — Loading
states.description: The Settings > AI page is loading AI configuration from the Rust backend via the get_ai_settings Tauri IPC command. A loading indicator is shown while data is fetched.

transitions.name: Settings loaded
transitions.description: AI settings loaded successfully from the backend, displaying the provider selection panel with four provider options

transitions.name: Load failed
transitions.description: Settings failed to load from the backend, showing an error message

states.name: AI Settings — Provider Selection
states.description: The AI settings page is loaded with the provider selection panel showing four options: Claude Code CLI, Claude API, Gemini CLI, and Gemini API. The currently selected provider's configuration section is expanded. The Test Connection and Save buttons are available.

transitions.name: Test connection
transitions.description: User clicks the Test Connection button, triggering a connection verification against the selected provider

transitions.name: Save settings
transitions.description: User clicks Save AI Settings, persisting the configuration to the Rust backend

states.name: AI Settings — Testing Connection
states.description: A connection test is in progress. The Test Connection button shows a loading spinner with 'Testing...' text. The test calls test_ai_connection via Tauri IPC.

transitions.name: Test completes
transitions.description: The connection test finishes (success or failure), displaying the result inline and returning to the provider selection state

states.name: AI Settings — Saving
states.description: Settings are being persisted to the backend. The Save button shows a loading spinner with 'Saving...' text.

transitions.name: Save succeeds
transitions.description: Settings saved successfully, showing a success banner and the Saved! button state

transitions.name: Save fails
transitions.description: Save operation fails, showing an error message

states.name: AI Settings — Saved Successfully
states.description: Settings were saved successfully. A green success banner with 'Settings saved successfully!' is displayed. The save button shows 'Saved!' with a check icon. This state auto-transitions after 3 seconds.

transitions.name: Success banner dismisses
transitions.description: The success banner auto-dismisses after 3 seconds, returning to the normal provider selection state

states.name: AI Settings — Error
states.description: An error occurred during loading or saving. A red error banner is displayed with the error message. The user can still interact with the provider selection controls.

transitions.name: User interacts with settings
transitions.description: User modifies a setting or retries, clearing the error state

states.name: Active Run — Iterating
states.description: An agentic verification workflow is currently running. The active dashboard shows live iteration progress with the current phase (verifying/working) and iteration count incrementing in real time. A Stop button is available to halt execution.

transitions.name: Goal achieved
transitions.description: The verification agent reports Pass with sufficient confidence for the required consecutive passes, and the loop exits successfully

transitions.name: Max iterations reached
transitions.description: The loop reaches max_iterations without achieving the goal

transitions.name: User stops run
transitions.description: User clicks the Stop button, halting the run after the current iteration completes

states.name: Run Complete — Goal Achieved
states.description: The agentic verification run completed successfully with goal_achieved:true. The run summary shows a green success indicator, iteration results with verdicts and confidence percentages, worker summaries, and token usage. A Continue button allows adding more sessions.

transitions.name: Continue run
transitions.description: User clicks the Continue button to add more sessions to the completed run

states.name: Run Complete — Max Iterations Reached
states.description: The run completed by hitting max_iterations without achieving the goal. The status shows 'Max iterations reached' or similar. The final verdict is typically Fail or Partial. A Continue button allows adding more sessions.

transitions.name: Continue run
transitions.description: User clicks the Continue button to add more sessions to the exhausted run

states.name: Run Complete — Stopped by User
states.description: The run was stopped by the user. The status indicates the run was stopped and shows iterations completed before the stop. A Continue button allows resuming.

transitions.name: Continue run
transitions.description: User clicks the Continue button to resume the stopped run

HTTP: GET /ui-bridge/sdk/console-errors (console errors for verifier context)
